doc.title: Don Albert and Herbert Hall Interview, 1978-08-03

title: Cities and states toured: Washington, Philadelphia, Midwest
summary: Howard Theater, Philadelphia home base, New Jersey, New York state, Ohio, Kentucky, Indiana.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Well, but I think it should be ready now. It's picking my voice up. What about Washington, D.C.? Were you ever in Washington?

Yeah, but we didn't play Washington. We just passed through. No, we played one day over there in Washington at that theater was there. I can't remember if I recall the name of the theater. It was the only Negro theater on the circuit that was similar to the Potter Theater. The Howard Theater. We played that one night. Well, that's a famous name around there.
Howard University. Well, Howard Theater. Well, Howard, Howard Theater.
That's a Nicholson's daughter is there.
If you remember him. Sure, I remember her.
I remember him too. Camilla, I think her name is.
Camilla.
Camilla.
Camilla. Camilla, yeah. I see.
But she should be real old if she's still living.
If she is. I don't know. She was there. But what about Baltimore, Maryland?
No, we didn't play Baltimore.
What about Philly? Philadelphia? Yeah.
We had a home base for a while.
Did you like it?
It was all right. Too much hilly country.
Pittsburgh?
Same way. Hilly country.
Trenton, New Jersey ever going to Trenton?
We played Trenton Newark in one other town in New Jersey. More of them every Sunday. Elizabeth? You're out of it? Atlantic City? Yeah, we played Atlantic City. I see.
Now, we've talked about New York quite a bit. What about on up from New York? Maine?
No, we played upstate New York. Vermont. Uh, Lance Falls, Albany. Vermont. Vermont. New Hampshire.
New York. New York. Massachusetts. New York. Connecticut. No. We had a bar with me that had one on the ass. Uh-huh. Billy Douglas.
Well, he's still alive. I don't know the last I heard he was in the town. Oh, no. He's out now. He is in jail. No, no. He's the last I heard he was alive. That hasn't been too long.
Yeah, I saw it in the, uh... They gave his address and everything from the International Association of Jazz Record Collectors. Well, I told Benny Carter about it.
Uh... Let me see now. We're covering the country. You mentioned Ohio. Yeah, we played the whole state of Ohio. Kentucky? Most of the city's in Kentucky. That's in the, uh, Hill Country also.
With the, uh, Hill Country. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh-huh.
About there with the stuff with Most of the cities in Kentucky. That's in the Hill Country also. But they all knock a hill. They're shooting and fighting. And half of them.
But they didn't have a shoot around. It was all peaceful. And then the people over in Indiana, what were they like?
Beautiful, beautiful. Indianapolis was a tremendous city. South Bend?
South Bend was all right. But Indianapolis stopped them all. Did they have many color people in Indiana?
Well, it was. And we played upstairs over the Indiana ballroom. And we played the theater there. I think it was the farthest. Big three of the time.
